entries.message: workflow has no "concurrency:", so every run of it executes at the same time even when a newer run supersedes the older ones. add a top-level "concurrency:" with a "group:" and "cancel-in-progress: true". use a group per pull request such as "${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}", so that a new push cancels only the older runs of the same pull request and not the runs of the others
"timeout-minutes" is not set at this job. Set it to avoid wasting runner minutes when the job hangs

neither the workflow nor this job sets "permissions:" so the GITHUB_TOKEN gets the default permissions of the repository. set "permissions:" at workflow-level or job-level (use "permissions: {}" for no permissions) because the "missing-permissions" rule is enabled
action "actions/checkout@v5" must be pinned to a full-length commit SHA like "{owner}/{repo}@{sha}" because the "unpinned-uses" rule is enabled

actions/checkout leaves the GITHUB_TOKEN in the git config of the workspace, where a later step such as an artifact upload can publish it. set "persist-credentials: false" under "with:" unless a later step needs to push

"github.base_ref" is a branch or tag name, which is not validated and can hold shell syntax. avoid using it directly in inline scripts. instead, pass it through an environment variable. see https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#good-practices-for-mitigating-script-injection-attacks for more details

swatinem/rust-cache restores a cache although the job runs "cargo publish", so a poisoned cache entry can end up in the published artifacts. remove this step or set "lookup-only: true", or set "cache-mode: none" on the job
"cargo publish" publishes to crates.io with the long-lived credential CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN. prefer trusted publishing with rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action and the permission "id-token: write"
